assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: discountForTripCount, countSingleTicketsInWindow, and discountForCategoryAndTripCount are three separate @TableTest methods.

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented — either as a row in the eligibility table or a separate note. It does not follow the ladder.
assertions.evidence: "Child gets a flat discount regardless of trips | CHILD | {1, 5, 40} | 20"

assertions.text: The discount ladder has multiple tiers derived from the 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundary values or value sets showing which ticket counts produce which discount. The maximum 40% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: "Exactly at the cap | 40 | 40" and "Beyond the cap stays capped | {41, 45, 100} | 40"

assertions.text: The 30-day rolling window boundary is tested: a ticket at exactly 30 days is included, at 31 days is excluded.
assertions.evidence: "Exactly 30 days ago is still in window | [30/SINGLE/ZONE_1] | 1" and "31 days ago has fallen out of the window | [31/SINGLE/ZONE_1] | 0"

assertions.text: The 30-day window is exercised at time-of-purchase granularity, not whole days only.
assertions.evidence: Only whole-day entries like "30/SINGLE/ZONE_1" and "31/SINGLE/ZONE_1" are used; description says 'Assumption: the boundary instant itself (exactly 30 days before purchaseTime) still counts as in-window' with no sub-day distinction.

assertions.text: Value sets in the tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount. No cross-tier contamination.
assertions.evidence: "Within first tier | {6, 7, 8, 9} | 5", "Within seventh tier | {36, 37, 38, 39} | 35" — all consistent with their tier.

assertions.text: The discount ladder table uses value sets for the ticket count column to group counts within the same tier — not one row per boundary value.
assertions.evidence: "Below first tier | {1, 2, 3, 4} | 0" and "Within second tier | {11, 12, 13, 14} | 10"

assertions.text: The tier-to-discount mapping is expressed once — not repeated across multiple tables.
assertions.evidence: discountForCategoryAndTripCount re-tests specific tier outputs ("Adult at a tier | ADULT | 10 | 10", "Adult and senior are capped the same | {ADULT, SENIOR} | 45 | 40") and calculatesDiscountEndToEnd again re-enumerates tier outputs (e.g. "Frequent rider with many recent trips ... | 10").

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 4 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the class or the tier method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express.
assertions.evidence: "The trip ladder: every 5th single ticket in the rolling 30-day window (counting the ticket being purchased now) raises the discount by 5%, up to a 40% cap."

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: The eligibility/passenger-type table includes a Zone column (or equivalent) with a value set to show that the discount applies regardless of zone.
assertions.evidence: discountForCategoryAndTripCount table columns are only "Scenario | Traveler Category | Trips In Window | Discount?" — no Zone column present.

assertions.text: The rolling-window counting concern shows by row that a past purchase's zone does not affect whether it counts toward the travel count
assertions.evidence: Zone does not affect the count | [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 2/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 3/SINGLE/ZONE_3] | 3

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set in at least one row
assertions.evidence: Adult and senior are capped the same | {ADULT, SENIOR} | 45 | 40

assertions.text: All 9 discount tiers are represented in the ladder table
assertions.evidence: Rows only cover 0,5,10,35,40 (missing 15,20,25,30): 'Exactly at second tier | 10 | 10' then jumps to 'Exactly at the seventh tier | 35 | 35'

assertions.text: Each tier expressed as a single row with a value set, not split across multiple rows
assertions.evidence: 'Exactly at first tier | 5 | 5' and 'Within first tier | {6, 7, 8, 9} | 5' split the 5% tier into two rows

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively rather than using absolute dates
assertions.evidence: [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 15/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 29/SINGLE/ZONE_1] ... daysAgo = Integer.parseInt(parts[0])

assertions.text: Multiple tables each addressing a distinct concern
assertions.evidence: discountForTripCount, countSingleTicketsInWindow, discountForCategoryAndTripCount, calculatesDiscountEndToEnd are separate @TableTest methods

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules
assertions.evidence: 'calculatesDiscountEndToEnd' re-covers child flat 20%, adult ladder tiers, and senior==adult already established in earlier tables

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable
assertions.evidence: Discount? varies across rows (0,5,10,35,40) and Count? varies (0,1,3,0) rather than staying constant

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body
assertions.evidence: 'Exactly 30 days ago is still in window | [30/SINGLE/ZONE_1] | 1' and '31 days ago has fallen out | [31/SINGLE/ZONE_1] | 0' make the boundary visible

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName or method name states what the code under test does
assertions.evidence: void discountForTripCount(...), void countSingleTicketsInWindow(...), void calculatesDiscountEndToEnd(...)

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on, and which the table holds constant for every row, must be visible as a column or named in the @DisplayName/@Description as deliberately held fixed.
assertions.evidence: PURCHASE_TIME is only used to derive relative 'days ago' offsets in the converter (PURCHASE_TIME.minusDays(daysAgo)), functioning as a fixed clock for input construction, not an outcome-determining constant; TravelerCategory.ADULT fixed in the converter corresponds to the explicitly out-of-scope child-exclusion rule.

assertions.text: When a title or description quantifies over a domain, the rows must actually cover that domain.
assertions.evidence: "Zone must never affect the count." is covered by rows using ZONE_1, ZONE_2, ZONE_3, e.g. "Zone does not affect the count | [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 2/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 3/SINGLE/ZONE_3]"; "CHILD always gets a flat 20% discount, independent of travel frequency" is covered by "Child gets a flat discount regardless of trips | CHILD | {1, 5, 40} | 20".
